questions.question: Which Part of the Indian Constitution deals with Panchayats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part IX**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part IX** of the **Indian Constitution** specifically addresses the **Panchayati Raj Institutions** (PRIs). It was constitutionally mandated to establish local self-government in rural areas.
 
• This part was officially inserted into the **Constitution of India** by the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**, which came into force on **April 24, 1993**.
 
• It consists of **Articles 243 to 243-O**, detailing the structure, composition, powers, and functions of **Panchayats**.
 
• The **73rd Amendment** also introduced the **11th Schedule**, which identifies **29 functional items** related to rural development, including agriculture, land improvement, and primary education, to be handled by the **Panchayats**.
 
• The provision mandates a **three-tier system** of **Panchayati Raj** at the **Village**, **Intermediate (Mandal)**, and **District** levels for states with a population exceeding 20 lakhs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Parts of the Constitution:**

 
 
• **Part V**: This part deals with **The Union**, encompassing the executive, legislature, and judiciary at the central level from **Articles 52 to 151**.
 
• **Part VII**: This part previously dealt with **States in Part B of the First Schedule** but was **repealed** by the **7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956**.
 
• **Part XI**: This part defines the **Relations between the Union and the States**, covering legislative and administrative aspects under **Articles 245 to 263**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Panchayati Raj:**
 
 
• **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957)**: Recommended the establishment of a three-tier **Panchayati Raj** system for the first time.
 
• **Rajasthan**: Was the first state to adopt the **Panchayati Raj** system in **Nagaur district** on **October 2, 1959**.
 
• **Article 40**: Located in the **Directive Principles of State Policy**, it initially directed the State to organize **Village Panchayats**.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment introduced 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections in education and jobs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**103rd Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019**, introduced a **10% reservation** for the **Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)** of citizens who are not covered under the existing reservation schemes for SCs, STs, and OBCs.
 
• This amendment modified the Indian Constitution by inserting **Article 15(6)** and **Article 16(6)** to permit the State to make special provisions for the advancement of economically weaker citizens.
 
• **Article 15(6)** enables the State to reserve up to 10% of seats in **educational institutions**, including private institutions, whether aided or unaided by the State, except for **minority educational institutions**.
 
• **Article 16(6)** empowers the State to provide a maximum of 10% reservation in **appointments or posts** in favor of any economically weaker section of citizens in addition to the existing reservations.
 
• The criteria for **EWS eligibility** are notified by the State from time to time based on family income and other indicators of **economic disadvantage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **98th Amendment**

 
 
• Enacted in **2012**, it inserted **Article 371J** to provide special provisions for the **Hyderabad-Karnataka region**, aiming to promote inclusive growth in backward districts of **Karnataka**.
 
 
 
• **102ⁿd Amendment**
 
 
• Passed in **2018**, it granted constitutional status to the **National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC)** and inserted **Article 338B** and **Article 342A** regarding the identification of socially and educationally backward classes.
 
 
 
• **104th Amendment**
 
 
• Enacted in **2020**, it extended the reservation of seats for **Scheduled Castes (SCs)** and **Scheduled Tribes (STs)** in the **Lok Sabha** and state assemblies for another 10 years, while discontinuing the reserved seats for the **Anglo-Indian community**.

questions.question: Who led the Ahom Revolt (1828–33) against British interference in Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gomdhar Konwar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ahom Revolt** of **1828** was the first significant organized uprising in **Assam** against the **British East India Company** following the conclusion of the first **Anglo-Burmese War**.
 
• After the signing of the **Treaty of Yandabo** in **1826**, the British failed to fulfill their promise of withdrawing from **Assam**, instead attempting to annex the territory into their administrative fold.
 
• **Gomdhar Konwar**, a prince of the **Ahom royal family**, emerged as the primary leader of the resistance, aiming to restore the **Ahom Monarchy** and end foreign interference.
 
• In **October 1828**, the rebels formally declared **Gomdhar Konwar** as the **Swargadeo** (Ahom King) at **Binnakuchi** and planned a military strike against the British station at **Jorhat**.
 
• The rebellion was bolstered by prominent Ahom officials and nobles, including **Dhanjay Borgohain** and **Jairam Khargharia Phukan**, who mobilized local levies to fight the colonial forces.
 
• The British military response, led by **Lieutenant Rutherford**, quickly suppressed the uprising; **Gomdhar Konwar** fled to the **Naga Hills** but was eventually captured and sentenced to imprisonment for treason.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maniram Dutta (Maniram Dewan)**:

 
 
• He was a sophisticated Assamese nobleman who originally served the British but later became a mastermind of the **Revolt of 1857** in **Assam**.
 
• He sought to restore **Kandarpeswar Singha** to the throne and was eventually executed by hanging in **1858** for his anti-British conspiracies.
 
 
 
• **Piyali Phukan**:
 
 
• He was a patriot who led a subsequent rebellion in **1830**, targeting the British military headquarters at **Rangpur**.
 
• Following the failure of this second major attempt at restoration, he was executed by the British, becoming a celebrated martyr of the **Assamese** freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **Treaty of Yandabo**:
 
 
• Signed on **February 24, 1826**, this treaty ended the **First Anglo-Burmese War** and resulted in **Burma** ceding **Assam**, **Manipur**, and **Arakan** to the British.

questions.question: As reiterated by the Supreme Court of India in September 2025, under which legislation does a Tribunal have the authority to order the eviction of a child from the property of a senior citizen in cases of failure to maintain them?

options.text: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2008
Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2009
Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2006

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007** was enacted to ensure the financial security, health, and welfare of elderly individuals in India. It mandates a legal obligation for children and heirs to provide maintenance to their parents.
 
• The **Supreme Court of India** and various High Courts have consistently interpreted the provisions of this Act to include the power of the **Maintenance Tribunal** to issue eviction orders. This is particularly applicable when children or legal heirs fail to maintain the senior citizen or occupy their property against their will, causing physical or mental distress.
 
• Under **Section 23** of the Act, any transfer of property by a senior citizen (via gift or otherwise) can be declared void by the **Tribunal** if the transferee fails to provide basic amenities and physical needs as promised.
 
• In recent judicial reiterations, the courts have clarified that while the Act does not explicitly use the word 'eviction' in its text, the **Right to Live with Dignity** and the definition of **Welfare** (under Section 2k) grant the Tribunal the authority to remove abusive or non-compliant children from the senior citizen's residence to ensure their protection.
 
• The Act provides a **summary procedure** for maintenance, meaning the **Tribunal** can pass orders relatively quickly compared to standard civil court proceedings, which is essential for the immediate relief of the elderly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007**:

 
 
• **Senior Citizen**: Defined as any person being a citizen of India who has attained the age of **60 years** or above.
 
• **Maintenance**: Includes provisions for food, clothing, residence, medical attendance, and treatment.
 
• **Tribunal Composition**: Each state government constitutes one or more **Maintenance Tribunals** for each sub-division, presided over by an officer not below the rank of **Sub-Divisional Officer** (SDO).
 
• **Maximum Maintenance**: The Act originally capped the monthly maintenance amount at **Rs. 10,000**, though several amendments and judicial reviews have sought to remove this ceiling based on the standard of living.
 
• **Appellate Tribunal**: Any senior citizen or parent aggrieved by the order of the Tribunal can prefer an appeal to the **Appellate Tribunal** within **60 days**.
 
• **Legal Representation**: One unique feature of this Act is that no party to a proceeding before a **Tribunal** or **Appellate Tribunal** shall be represented by a legal practitioner, ensuring a simplified and direct process.

questions.question: Which three indicators are considered while calculating the Human Development Index (HDI)?

options.text: Life expectancy, education, and per capita income
Foreign exchange reserves, literacy rate, and poverty rate
GDP, inflation rate, and unemployment rate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Life expectancy, education, and per capita income**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a summary composite measure of average achievement in key dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life, being knowledgeable, and having a decent standard of living.
 
• The health dimension is assessed by **Life Expectancy at Birth**, which estimates the number of years a newborn is expected to live based on current mortality rates.
 
• The education dimension is measured by combining the **Mean Years of Schooling** for adults aged 25 years and older and the **Expected Years of Schooling** for children of school-entering age.
 
• The standard of living dimension is measured by **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita**, adjusted for **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** in international dollars to account for differences in the cost of living across countries.
 
• The **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** publishes the **Human Development Report** annually, ranking countries based on their HDI score, which ranges from **0 to 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Origin of HDI**:

 
 
• It was created by Pakistani economist **Mahbub ul Haq** and Indian economist **Amartya Sen** in **1990** to shift the focus of development economics from national income accounting to people-centered policies.
 
 
 
• **Other Indices in the Human Development Report**:
 
 
• **Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI)**: Adjusts the HDI for inequality in the distribution of each dimension across the population.
 
• **Gender Inequality Index (GII)**: Measures gender disparities in reproductive health, empowerment, and labor market participation.
 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**: Identifies multiple deprivations at the household and individual level in health, education, and standard of living.
 
 
 
• **Categorization**:
 
 
• Countries are categorized into four groups based on their scores: **Very High** (0.800 and above), **High** (0.700 to 0.799), **Medium** (0.550 to 0.699), and **Low Human Development** (below 0.550).

questions.question: In Google Docs, when you press Ctrl + S, what technical action occurs in the background?

options.text: The document is saved to local storage
An immediate sync to Drive is triggered
The keyboard shortcut is not recognized
The Save As dialog box appears on screen

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**An immediate sync to Drive is triggered**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Google Docs** is a **cloud-based** word processor that utilizes **asynchronous** data transmission to save changes in real-time as a user types.
 
• While the application features an **Auto-save** mechanism that periodically pushes data to the server, pressing **Ctrl + S** acts as a manual trigger to force the **synchronization process** immediately.
 
• Technically, this action sends a request to the **Google Drive servers** to ensure that the latest buffer of edits is committed to the cloud storage and reflected in the **Version History**.
 
• Upon pressing the shortcut, the status message near the document title usually transitions from **Saving...** to **All changes saved to Drive**, confirming that the handshake between the browser and the **remote server** is complete.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cloud Architecture and Storage**:

 
 
• Unlike legacy software that writes data to a **local Hard Disk Drive (HDD)**, Google Docs stores data within the **Google Cloud Platform** infrastructure.
 
• The **Ctrl + S** shortcut in web apps is often a **legacy habit** for users transitioning from desktop environments like **Microsoft Word**, where manual saving is critical to prevent data loss from system crashes.
 
 
 
• **Collaborative Environment**:
 
 
• Immediate syncing ensures that other **collaborators** viewing the same document see the most recent updates with minimal **latency**.
 
• The **Real-time Presence** feature relies on these constant sync triggers to maintain consistency across multiple user sessions.
 
 
 
• **Offline Functionality**:
 
 
• If **Offline Mode** is enabled via the **Google Docs Offline extension**, pressing **Ctrl + S** saves the changes to the browser's **IndexedDB** or **Local Storage** until a network connection allows for a server sync.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the role of the Windows operating system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Managing files and folders**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Microsoft Windows** is a widely used **Operating System (OS)** that serves as the essential layer of software managing communication between the user and the **computer hardware**.
 
• One of the fundamental responsibilities of any operating system, including Windows, is **File Management**, which involves the organized storage, retrieval, and naming of data on storage devices.
 
• Windows utilizes a **hierarchical file system** structure where data is stored in **files**, and these files are grouped into **folders** (also known as directories) to maintain an orderly environment.
 
• The **File Explorer** is the native utility in Windows that provides a **Graphical User Interface (GUI)** for users to perform critical tasks such as **creating**, **moving**, **renaming**, **copying**, and **deleting** files and folders.
 
• Behind the scenes, the operating system manages **file allocation tables** or **NTFS (New Technology File System)** metadata to keep track of exactly where bits of data are physically located on **Hard Disk Drives (HDD)** or **Solid State Drives (SSD)**.
 
• Beyond organization, the OS ensures **data security** by managing **file permissions** and attributes, deciding which users or programs have the right to read, write, or execute specific files.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Understanding Application vs. System Software**:

 
 
• **Designing multimedia presentations**: This is an **application-level task** performed using specialized software like **Microsoft PowerPoint** or **Google Slides**, which runs on top of the operating system.
 
• **Editing audio files**: This requires dedicated **Digital Audio Workstations (DAW)** or editors such as **Audacity** or **Adobe Audition**; the OS provides the resources (CPU/RAM) for these tools but does not perform the editing itself.
 
• **Playing games**: While Windows is a premier platform for gaming due to its **DirectX API** and **driver support**, the actual execution of game logic is the function of the game application, not the primary role of the OS.
 
 
 
• **Other Core Functions of Windows**:
 
 
• **Memory Management**: Efficiently allocating **Random Access Memory (RAM)** to different running processes.
 
• **Processor Management**: Handling the **scheduling** of tasks to ensure the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)** is utilized optimally.
 
• **Device Management**: Using **Device Drivers** to facilitate communication with peripherals like printers, keyboards, and monitors.

questions.question: Solar energy is globally measured in the unit of KWh. The physical quantity corresponding to the unit KWh is _____________.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The unit **Kilowatt-hour (kWh)** is the standard commercial unit used to measure the total amount of **Electric energy** consumed or generated over a specific period of time.
 
• Physical quantity **Power** is defined as the rate of energy consumption or transfer, expressed as **Power = Energy ÷ Time**.
 
• By rearranging the formula, **Energy** is calculated as the product of power and time (**Energy = Power × Time**); since **Kilowatt** is a unit of power and **Hour** is a unit of time, their product represents energy.
 
• In the context of **Solar energy** systems, the output of **Photovoltaic (PV)** panels is measured in **kWh** to quantify the total electrical work performed or electricity produced by the system globally.

• **Electric charge**:

 
 
• The physical property of matter that causes it to experience a force in an electromagnetic field, measured in **Coulombs (C)**.
 
• It is the product of current and time (Q = I × t).
 
 
 
• **Current**:
 
 
• The rate of flow of electric charge through a conductor, with the **Ampere (A)** as its SI unit.
 
• 1 Ampere is equivalent to the flow of 1 **Coulomb** of charge per second.
 
 
 
• **Force**:
 
 
• A vector quantity that causes an object to change its velocity, measured in **Newtons (N)**.
 
• It is defined by **Newton's Second Law** as mass multiplied by acceleration (F = m × a).

questions.question: Which landmark case is credited with relaxing the rule of locus standi and establishing the foundation for Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in India?

options.text: Minerva Mills vs. Union of India
Maneka Gandhi vs. Union of India
S.P. Gupta vs. Union of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**S.P. Gupta vs. Union of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The landmark case of **S.P. Gupta vs. Union of India (1981)**, popularly known as the **First Judges Case**, is fundamentally credited with the relaxation of the traditional rule of **Locus Standi**.
 
• The Supreme Court, through a bench led by **Justice P.N. Bhagwati**, ruled that any member of the public or a social action group acting bona fide can approach the court to seek judicial redress for a person or class of persons who, due to poverty, disability, or a socially disadvantaged position, cannot approach the court themselves.
 
• By allowing third parties to represent the interests of the marginalized, the judgment established the procedural foundation for **Public Interest Litigation (PIL)** in the Indian judicial system.
 
• The court emphasized that the **Rule of Law** requires that legal injury to a person or group should not go unredressed simply because they lack the means to navigate the legal process.
 
• This shift transformed the Indian judiciary from a passive arbiter of private disputes into an active protector of **Fundamental Rights** and social justice, making justice more accessible to the common man.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Minerva Mills vs. Union of India (1980)**

 
 
• This case is pivotal for the **Basic Structure Doctrine**, where the court struck down clauses of the **42nd Amendment Act** that sought to give **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** absolute precedence over **Fundamental Rights**.
 
• It established that the power of the Parliament to amend the Constitution is limited and **Judicial Review** is an essential feature of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Golaknath vs. State of Punjab (1967)**
 
 
• The Supreme Court held that the Parliament does not have the power to curtail or take away any of the **Fundamental Rights** through constitutional amendments.
 
• It introduced the doctrine of **Prospective Overruling**, ensuring that the judgment did not invalidate previous amendments but restricted future ones.
 
 
 
• **Maneka Gandhi vs. Union of India (1978)**
 
 
• This case expanded the horizon of **Article 21** (Right to Life and Personal Liberty) by ruling that any 'procedure established by law' must be just, fair, and reasonable, and not arbitrary.
 
• It linked **Article 14, 19, and 21**, creating the **Golden Triangle** of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: When was Oil India Limited (OIL) incorporated as a company?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1959**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oil India Limited (OIL)** was officially incorporated as a private limited company on **February 18, 1959**.
 
• The company was established as a joint venture between the **Government of India** and the **Burmah Oil Company Limited** (a British entity) to explore and develop oil resources in **Northeast India**.
 
• The incorporation followed the significant discovery of oil fields in **Nahorkatiya** (1953) and **Moran** (1956) in the state of **Assam**, which necessitated a specialized corporate body for management.
 
• Initially, the headquarters was located in **Shillong**, but the operational base was later moved to **Duliajan**, Assam, to be closer to the production sites.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Corporate Evolution and Nationalization:
 
 
• In **1961**, the equity structure was revised to a **50:50** partnership between the **Government of India** and **Burmah Oil Company**.
 
• On **October 14, 1981**, the company became a fully-owned **Government of India Enterprise** under the **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas**.
 
• OIL was granted the **Navratna** status in **2010** and was further elevated to the **Maharatna** category in **August 2023**.
 
 
 
• Infrastructural Contributions:

questions.question: Which of the following substances is considered neutral according to the pH scale?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pure water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **pH scale** is a logarithmic measurement used to specify the acidity or basicity of an aqueous solution, originally developed by Danish biochemist **S.P.L. Sørensen** in **1909**.
 
• A substance is defined as **neutral** when it possesses a pH value of exactly **7.0** at a standard temperature of **25°C (298 K)**.
 
• **Pure water** is the primary reference for neutrality because it undergoes **auto-ionization**, where the concentration of **hydrogen ions (H⁺)** is exactly equal to the concentration of **hydroxide ions (OH−)**.
 
• At equilibrium in pure water, the concentration of these ions is **1.0 × 10−⁷ moles per liter**, resulting in a state where neither acidic nor basic characteristics are dominant.
 
• The scale ranges from **0 to 14**, where values **below 7** indicate an **acidic** nature (high H⁺ concentration) and values **above 7** indicate a **basic** or **alkaline** nature (high OH− concentration).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stomach acid**

 
 
• Mainly consists of **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** produced by the stomach lining.
 
• It typically has a very low pH range of **1.5 to 3.5**, which is crucial for activating **digestive enzymes** and killing ingested bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Sea water**
 
 
• Functions as a complex chemical solution with a slightly **alkaline** pH generally ranging from **7.5 to 8.4**.
 
• Its pH is stabilized by the **bicarbonate buffer system**, though it is susceptible to **ocean acidification** due to rising atmospheric **CO₂** levels.
 
 
 
• **Lime juice**
 
 
• Contains high concentrations of **citric acid**, typically between **5% to 6%** by weight.
 
• This high acid content results in a low pH value of approximately **2.0 to 2.8**, making it significantly more acidic than neutral solutions.

questions.question: How many Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) are there in the Indian Parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**24**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The system of **Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs)** was first inaugurated in the **Indian Parliament** in **April 1993** based on the recommendation of the **Rules Committee**.
 
• Initially, there were **17 committees** established to cover various ministries and departments of the **Union Government**.
 
• On **July 20, 2004**, the **Parliament** expanded the committee system, increasing the total number of **DRSCs** from **17 to 24**.
 
• Among the **24 committees**, **16 committees** function under the administrative control of the **Speaker of the Lok Sabha**, and **8 committees** function under the **Chairman of the Rajya Sabha**.
 
• The main objective of these committees is to ensure the **accountability** of the **Executive** to the **Legislature**, especially in terms of **financial expenditure** and **policy implementation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Composition and Membership**:

 
 
• Each **Departmentally Related Standing Committee** consists of **31 members** in total.
 
• Out of these 31 members, **21** are nominated from the **Lok Sabha** and **10** are nominated from the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• The **Speaker** of the Lok Sabha and the **Chairman** of the Rajya Sabha nominate the members from their respective houses based on the **proportional representation** of political parties.
 
 
 
• **Tenure and Eligibility**:
 
 
• The term of office for the members of these committees is **one year**.
 
• A **Minister** cannot be a member of any **Standing Committee**; if a member is appointed as a minister, they must vacate their seat in the committee.
 
 
 
• **Functions**:
 
 
• The committees examine the **Demands for Grants** made by various ministries before they are voted upon in the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• They scrutinize **Bills** referred to them by the presiding officers and consider **Annual Reports** of the ministries.
 
• They also evaluate long-term **National Policy Documents** presented to the **Parliament**.

questions.question: When lemon juice is added to milk, it forms paneer. This process is known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coagulation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Milk is a **colloidal solution** where protein particles, specifically **Casein**, are suspended and prevented from clumping by negative electrical charges.
 
• When an acidic substance like **lemon juice** (which contains **citric acid**) is added, the **hydrogen ions** (H⁺) neutralize the negative charges on the protein molecules.
 
• As the **pH** of the milk drops towards its **isoelectric point** (approximately 4.6 for casein), the proteins lose their repulsive forces and begin to aggregate.
 
• The process of these particles clumping together to transform a liquid into a thickened mass or solid is scientifically defined as **Coagulation** or **Curdling**.
 
• In the preparation of **paneer**, this coagulation results in the separation of solid **curds** from the liquid **whey**, which is then filtered and pressed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sedimentation**:

 
 
• It is a physical process where **insoluble solids** settle at the bottom of a liquid due to the influence of **gravity**.
 
• It is commonly used in **water treatment** to remove sand, silt, and clay particles from raw water.
 
 
 
• **Hydrolysis**:
 
 
• It is a **chemical reaction** involving the breaking of a bond in a molecule using a **water molecule**.
 
• In biological systems, enzymes facilitate the hydrolysis of **polymers** (like starch or proteins) into smaller **monomers** during the process of digestion.
 
 
 
• **Crystallization**:
 
 
• It is the process by which a **solid forms**, where the atoms or molecules are highly organized into a structure known as a **crystal lattice**.
 
• This technique is widely used in laboratories and industries to **purify** substances, such as obtaining pure sugar from cane juice or salt from seawater.

questions.question: Which of the following Chola rulers is credited with building a powerful navy and conquering Sri Lanka, Maldives, and Lakshadweep?

• **Rajaraja I**, who reigned from **985 CE to 1014 CE**, is considered the primary architect of the **Imperial Chola** maritime empire, transforming the kingdom into a dominant sea power.
 
• He established a **powerful navy** that allowed the Cholas to assert control over the **Bay of Bengal** and the **Arabian Sea**, facilitating trade with the **Song Dynasty** of China and Southeast Asian kingdoms.
 
• During his military campaigns, he conquered the **Northern part of Sri Lanka** (then known as **Ilam**), destroyed the capital **Anuradhapura**, and established a new Chola province with **Polonnaruwa** as its headquarters.
 
• His naval expeditions reached the **Maldives**, which are referred to in Chola inscriptions as **Munnir Palantivu Pannirayiram** (the twelve thousand ancient islands of the sea), and the **Lakshadweep** islands.
 
• The naval strength developed under his reign laid the crucial foundation for his son, **Rajendra I**, to launch even more ambitious trans-oceanic expeditions to **Southeast Asia**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajendra I**:

 
 
• He was the son of **Rajaraja I** and expanded the empire to its greatest extent, conquering the **entire island of Sri Lanka** and reaching the **Ganges River**.
 
• He is famous for his naval raid on the **Srivijaya Empire** (modern-day Indonesia and Malaysia) in **1025 CE** to protect Chola trade interests.
 
 
 
• **Vijayalaya**:
 
 
• He was the founder of the **Imperial Chola Dynasty** who captured **Thanjavur** from the **Muttaraiyar** in approximately **850 CE**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in the four official meteorological seasons of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Spring season**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)**, which is the principal government agency responsible for meteorological observations and weather forecasting, officially recognizes four distinct meteorological seasons in India.
 
• The four official seasons are: the **Winter season** (December to February), the **Summer season** or Pre-monsoon (March to May), the **Rainy season** or Southwest Monsoon (June to September), and the **Post-monsoon season** (October to November).
 
• **Spring season** (traditionally known as **Vasant**) is part of the traditional Indian **Shada-Ritu** (six seasons) calendar, but it is not classified as an independent meteorological season by the **IMD** for climate reporting and administrative data.
 
• Meteorologically, the period associated with spring is transitionary and is typically absorbed within the latter half of the **Winter season** and the onset of the **Pre-monsoon/Summer** period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Summer season**:

 
 
• Known as the **Hot Weather Season**, it occurs from **March to May** as the sun moves northward toward the **Tropic of Cancer**.
 
• Characteristic features include the **Loo** (hot, dry winds) in **Northern India** and pre-monsoon showers such as **Mango Showers** in **Karnataka** and **Kerala**.
 
 
 
• **Rainy season**:
 
 
• Identified as the **Southwest Monsoon Season** (June to September), it provides nearly **75%** of India's annual rainfall.
 
• The monsoon usually sets in over the **Kerala coast** by early **June** and covers the entire country by mid-July.
 
 
 
• **Winter season**:
 
 
• Designated as the **Cold Weather Season** from **December to February**.
 
• It is marked by clear skies and the influence of **Western Disturbances**, which bring rainfall to the **North-West** plains and snow to the **Himalayas**.

__
 
• The **Kensington Treaty** (formally known as the **UK-Germany Defence Treaty**) is a landmark security agreement signed in **January 2025** to enhance military and industrial cooperation.
 
• It represents the most significant bilateral defense pact between the **United Kingdom** and **Germany** since **World War II**, aiming to solidify the European pillar within **NATO**.
 
• The treaty facilitates **joint procurement** of advanced weaponry, including the development of new **long-range strike missiles** and high-precision artillery systems.
 
• A major economic outcome of the treaty is the establishment of a specialized **artillery gun barrel factory** in the UK, marking the first time in ten years that such barrels will be manufactured domestically.
 
• The agreement includes provisions for **maritime security**, allowing German **P-8 Poseidon** aircraft to operate from **RAF Lossiemouth** in Scotland to monitor hostile activity in the **North Atlantic**.
 
• It focuses heavily on the protection of **critical underwater infrastructure**, such as data cables and energy pipelines, against sabotage or hybrid threats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trinity House Agreement**:

 
 
• This was the foundational defense pact signed in **October 2024** that paved the way for the full 2025 treaty.
 
• It established the framework for **industrial collaboration** and synchronized military exercises between the **British Army** and the **Bundeswehr**.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Implications**:
 
 
• The treaty aligns the two largest defense spenders in **Europe**, creating a deterrent against regional aggression.
 
• It complements existing agreements like the **Lancaster House Treaties** (UK-France) and the **Aachen Treaty** (Germany-France), forming a strategic defense triangle.
 
 
 
• **Joint Air Defense**:
 
 
• The pact emphasizes **interoperability** between the **Royal Air Force (RAF)** and the **Luftwaffe**, particularly in **integrated air and missile defense** systems.

questions.question: The Banarasi, Patiala and Lucknow Gharanas are associated with which of the following musical styles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thumri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thumri** is a prominent **semi-classical** vocal form of **Hindustani Classical Music**, characterized by its lyrical focus on romantic and devotional themes, particularly the divine love of **Radha** and **Krishna**.
 
• The **Lucknow Gharana** played a pivotal role in the evolution of **Thumri**, reaching its peak under the patronage of **Nawab Wajid Ali Shah** in the 19th century. This style is often linked with **Kathak** dance, emphasizing expressive gestures (Abhinaya) and grace.
 
• The **Banaras Gharana** (Varanasi) is famous for the **Bol Banav** style of **Thumri**. This tradition focuses on the melodic elaboration of words to evoke deep emotional meaning. Renowned vocalists like **Girija Devi** and **Siddheshwari Devi** are the pillars of this gharana.
 
• The **Patiala Gharana** is distinguished by the **Patiala-Ang** of **Thumri**, which was revolutionized by **Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan**. It is known for its intricate vocal ornamentations like **Murkis**, **Khatkas**, and its fusion of **Tappa**-like agility with soulful melody.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tappa**:

 
 
• A vocal style derived from the folksongs of **camel riders** in the **Punjab** region.
 
• It is known for its extremely rapid and complex **Taans** and was refined by **Shori Mian** of the **Lucknow** court.
 
 
 
• **Kajari**:
 
 
• A popular **seasonal folk song** of **Uttar Pradesh** and **Bihar**, traditionally sung during the **monsoon** season.
 
• While frequently performed by **Banaras** vocalists, it is classified as a **folk-based** genre rather than the defining classical style of the three gharanas.
 
 
 
• **Chaiti**:
 
 
• A semi-classical song performed during the Hindu month of **Chait** (March-April), often associated with the **Rama Navami** festival.
 
• It belongs to the same **Purvanchal** musical tradition as **Kajari** and **Thumri** but remains a seasonal specific sub-genre.

questions.question: The Atal Tunnel is built in which Himalayan range?

questions.question: In basketball, what does the term “triple-double” signify?

options.text: Achieving double the points, rebounds, and assists in a single game
Making three consecutive dunks in a game
Recording double digits in three statistical categories
Committing three technical fouls in a match

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Recording double digits in three statistical categories**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **triple-double** is a performance in which a basketball player accumulates a **double-digit total** (10 or more) in **three** of five statistical categories.
 
• The five statistical categories officially tracked for this achievement are **points**, **total rebounds**, **assists**, **steals**, and **blocked shots**.
 
• The most common combination achieved by players involves **points**, **rebounds**, and **assists**, reflecting a high level of **versatility** on the court.
 
• The term was popularized in the **1980s**, specifically to describe the all-around impact of players like **Magic Johnson**, who could facilitate, score, and rebound effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Related Statistical Terms**:

 
 
• **Double-Double**: This occurs when a player reaches double digits in **two** of the five categories. It is a common occurrence for elite **NBA** players.
 
• **Quadruple-Double**: Reaching double digits in **four** categories. This is extremely rare and has only been officially recorded four times in **NBA** history by **Nate Thurmond**, **Alvin Robertson**, **Hakeem Olajuwon**, and **David Robinson**.
 
• **Quintuple-Double**: Achieving double digits in all **five** categories. This feat has never been recorded in **NBA** history.
 
 
 
• **Notable Record Holders**:
 
 
• **Russell Westbrook** holds the record for the most career triple-doubles in **NBA** history, surpassing the long-standing record of **Oscar Robertson**.
 
• **Nikola Jokic** is another modern player known for high frequency in recording triple-doubles from the **Center** position.
 
 
 
• **Rules Context**:
 
 
• In the **NBA**, committing **two technical fouls** results in an automatic ejection, making the notion of three technical fouls irrelevant to a positive performance metric.

questions.question: A national emergency must be approved by Parliament within ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30 Days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 352** of the **Indian Constitution** empowers the **President** to proclaim a **National Emergency** when the security of India or any part of its territory is threatened by **war**, **external aggression**, or **armed rebellion**.
 
• A proclamation of **National Emergency** must be approved by both the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha** within **one month** (which is equivalent to **30 days**) from the date of its issue.
 
• Prior to the **44th Amendment Act of 1978**, the period allowed for parliamentary approval was **two months**; however, this timeframe was reduced to ensure stricter legislative control over executive powers.
 
• If the **proclamation** is issued at a time when the **Lok Sabha** has been dissolved or the dissolution takes place during the **30-day** period without approval, the proclamation survives until **30 days** from the first sitting of the **reconstituted Lok Sabha**, provided the **Rajya Sabha** has approved it in the meantime.
 
• Once approved, the **Emergency** continues for **six months** and can be extended for an indefinite period with periodic parliamentary approval every six months via a **special majority**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Grounds and Procedure**:

 
 
• The **President** can only declare a **National Emergency** after receiving a **written recommendation** from the **Cabinet** (the Prime Minister and other ministers of cabinet rank), a safeguard added by the **44th Amendment**.
 
• The **special majority** required for approval consists of a **majority of the total membership** of each House and a majority of not less than **two-thirds of the members** present and voting.
 
 
 
• **Other Emergency Provisions**:
 
 
• **Article 356 (President's Rule)**: Relates to the failure of constitutional machinery in states. It must be approved by Parliament within **two months** (60 days) and lasts for six months at a time.
 
• **Article 360 (Financial Emergency)**: Declared when the financial stability or credit of India is threatened. It also requires parliamentary approval within **two months** (60 days) and remains in force indefinitely until revoked.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding RAM and ROM and select the correct option.

(i) ROM is faster than RAM because it stores permanent system instructions accessed less frequently by the CPU.

(ii) RAM can be read from and written to by the CPU, but its contents are erased when the power is turned off.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(i) False, (ii) True**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Statement (i) claims that **ROM** is faster than **RAM**; however, in standard computer architecture, **RAM** is significantly faster than **ROM**. **RAM** is designed for high-speed data exchange with the **CPU** to handle active processes, whereas **ROM** is used for permanent storage of **firmware** and has much slower data transfer rates. ***Hence, statement (i) is incorrect.***
 
• Statement (ii) identifies **RAM** as memory that supports both **read and write** operations, which is essential for the **CPU** to process and update data in real-time. It also correctly states that **RAM** is **volatile**, meaning all data is lost when the **power supply** is cut off. ***Hence, statement (ii) is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Random Access Memory (RAM)**:

 
 
• Acts as the **primary memory** or **main memory** of a computer.
 
• Includes **DRAM (Dynamic RAM)**, which is used for system memory, and **SRAM (Static RAM)**, which is faster and used for the **CPU Cache**.
 
• Its capacity directly impacts the **multi-tasking** capabilities and overall speed of the system.
 
 
 
• **Read-Only Memory (ROM)**:
 
 
• It is **non-volatile**, meaning it retains instructions like the **BIOS (Basic Input/Output System)** or **UEFI** even without power.
 
• The **Bootstrap Loader**, which starts the operating system during the **booting process**, is stored here.
 
• Modern versions include **EEPROM**, which can be erased and rewritten using electrical charges, and **Mask ROM**, which is programmed during manufacturing.

questions.question: Which tool is most commonly used by the Reserve Bank of India to regulate liquidity in the economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Repo rate adjustment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Repo Rate**, or Repurchase Rate, is the key benchmark interest rate at which the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** lends short-term money to commercial banks against the collateral of government securities.
 
• It serves as the primary instrument of the **Monetary Policy** to regulate **liquidity**, control inflation, and ensure price stability in the Indian economy.
 
• When the **RBI** aims to reduce excess liquidity and curb inflation, it increases the **Repo Rate**, making borrowing expensive for banks, which subsequently raises lending rates for the public and reduces the **money supply**.
 
• To stimulate economic growth during a slowdown, the **RBI** decreases the **Repo Rate**, providing cheaper credit to banks and encouraging investment and consumption.
 
• Decisions regarding the **Repo Rate** are made by the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**, which typically meets bi-monthly to review the macroeconomic situation and adjust the **Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF)** corridor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Policy Tools** (Managed by the Government of India):

 
 
• **Fiscal Stimulus**: This refers to **budgetary measures** like increased government spending or tax reductions designed to revive the economy; it is not a direct tool of the **RBI**.
 
• **Government Subsidies**: These are financial grants provided by the state to reduce the cost of essential goods (like fertilizers or food), functioning as a **fiscal transfer** rather than a monetary liquidity tool.
 
 
 
• **Trade and Revenue Tools**:
 
 
• **Tariff Imposition**: These are customs duties or taxes placed on imported goods to protect domestic industries or generate revenue, managed by the **Ministry of Finance** and **Ministry of Commerce**.
 
 
 
• **Other RBI Monetary Instruments**:
 
 
• **Reverse Repo Rate**: The rate at which the **RBI** absorbs liquidity from banks by borrowing from them.
 
• **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)**: A specific portion of a bank's **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)** that must be maintained with the **RBI** in cash.

questions.question: When was the Telugu language declared as a classical language of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2008**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Telugu language** was officially declared as a **Classical Language** by the **Government of India** in the year **2008**.
 
• The formal announcement was issued by the **Union Ministry of Culture** on **October 31, 2008**, acknowledging the language’s profound historical and literary significance.
 
• Alongside **Telugu**, the **Kannada language** was also granted the same status in **2008** after fulfilling the specific criteria set by the linguistic expert committee.
 
• The recognition followed a long-standing demand by scholars and the state government of **Andhra Pradesh**, providing evidence of the language’s antiquity and its original literary tradition.
 
• Eligibility for this status requires a language to have a recorded history of early texts spanning at least **1500 to 2000 years**, a condition that **Telugu** successfully satisfied through its ancient inscriptions and poetic works.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classical Language Criteria**:

 
 
• High antiquity of early texts and recorded history over a period of **1500–2000 years**.
 
• A body of ancient literature or texts considered a valuable heritage by generations of speakers.
 
• The literary tradition must be original and not borrowed from another speech community.
 
• A distinction must exist between the classical language and its modern or later forms.
 
 
 
• **List of Classical Languages**:
 
 
• **Tamil**: The first language to be accorded the status in **2004**.
 
• **Sanskrit**: Declared in **2005**.
 
• **Malayalam**: Accorded status in **2013**.
 
• **Odia**: Declared in **2014**.
 
• **Recent Additions (2024)**: The Cabinet recently approved **Marathi**, **Assamese**, **Bengali**, **Pali**, and **Prakrit** as classical languages.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Status**: Two major international awards for scholars of eminence in the language and the establishment of a **Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Languages**.

questions.question: The earliest evidence of stone tools in India has been found at:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Attirampakkam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Attirampakkam**, located in the **Kortallayar River Basin** near **Chennai**, **Tamil Nadu**, is recognized as one of the most significant **Paleolithic** archaeological sites in India.
 
• Extensive excavations led by **Shanti Pappu** and her team from the **Sharma Centre for Heritage Education** have revealed a continuous sequence of prehistoric cultures at this location.
 
• The site is famous for providing the earliest scientifically dated evidence of **Acheulian** stone tools in the Indian subcontinent, using **cosmogenic nuclide burial dating**.
 
• The findings indicate that **hominins** were present in South Asia and producing **handaxes** and **cleavers** as far back as approximately **1.51 million years ago** (mya).
 
• This discovery at **Attirampakkam** challenged previous theories about the **Out of Africa** migration, suggesting that early humans reached India much earlier than the previously estimated 0.5 mya.
 
• The stone tools recovered from the site were primarily fashioned from **quartzite**, exhibiting sophisticated **bifacial** flaking techniques typical of the **Lower Paleolithic** era.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lothal**:

 
 
• Situated in the **Saragwala** village of **Gujarat**, it was a major city of the **Indus Valley Civilization**.
 
• It flourished during the **Bronze Age** (c. 2400−1900 BCE) and is renowned for the world's earliest known **artificial dockyard**.
 
 
 
• **Hunsgi Valley**:
 
 
• Located in the **Yadgir** district of **Karnataka**, it is another vital **Lower Paleolithic** site in India.
 
• Early humans in this region notably used **limestone** to manufacture their stone tools, providing insight into the adaptation to local geological resources.
 
 
 
• **Mehrgarh**:
 
 
• Located on the **Kacchi Plain** of **Balochistan**, **Pakistan**, it is one of the earliest **Neolithic** sites in the world.
 
• It dates back to roughly **7000 BCE** and provides foundational evidence of the transition from hunting-gathering to **agriculture** and **animal domestication** in South Asia.

questions.question: Who wrote the iconic nationalist novel *Anandamath*?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anandamath** is a seminal Bengali novel written by **Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay** and was first published in **1882**.
 
• The novel is set in the background of the **Sannyasi Rebellion** of the late 18th century and the **Great Bengal Famine of 1770**, depicting the struggle of ascetic warriors against British colonial rule.
 
• It is most famous for containing the hymn **Vande Mataram**, which later became the **National Song of India** and served as a powerful rallying cry for the Indian independence movement.
 
• The work is credited with popularizing the concept of **Bharat Mata** (Mother India), personifying the nation as a mother figure requiring liberation from foreign oppression.
 
• The narrative focuses on a secret society called **Santan Dal** (Children’s Army) that fights against the tyranny of the British East India Company and its administrative failures during the famine.
 
• Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay is often referred to as **Sahitya Samrat** (Emperor of Literature) in Bengali for his profound impact on Indian literature and nationalism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay**:

 
 
• A renowned novelist known for portraying the struggles of rural society and female protagonists in works like **Devdas**, **Parineeta**, and **Srikanta**.
 
• His novel **Pather Dabi** was banned by the British government for its revolutionary nationalist content.
 
 
 
• **Dinabandhu Mitra**:
 
 
• A Bengali dramatist best known for his play **Nil Darpan** (1860), which exposed the brutal exploitation of indigo farmers by British planters.
 
 
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore**:
 
 
• The first non-European to win the **Nobel Prize in Literature** (1913) for **Gitanjali**.
 
• He composed the national anthems of both **India** (Jana Gana Mana) and **Bangladesh** (Amar Shonar Bangla).
